I notice you haven't provided the initial symptoms yet, but based on your profile, you mentioned a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities along with low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To better understand your condition, how long have these symptoms been present?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
REQUEST IMAGES: Rash_photo

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC - Normal, Hemoglobin - Normal, Platelets - Slightly elevated; Rash_photo - Image not provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: That's helpful; the normal white blood cell count suggests this might not be a typical bacterial infection. Have you noticed any joint pain, sore throat, or redness in your eyes alongside the rash?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)

The classic "slapped cheek" facial rash that spares the perioral area, combined with a subsequent pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, followed by symptoms of a viral upper respiratory infection, strongly points to this diagnosis. Do you notice any lacy, reticular patterns appearing on her wrists or ankles?
